skill.name: git-guardrails-claude-code
skill.description: Set up Claude Code hooks that block destructive Git commands before they execute, including push, hard reset, clean, branch deletion, and workspace restore commands.
skill.summary: Install Claude Code Git guardrails that stop risky Git commands before execution.
skill.author: mattpocock

security_audit.summary: The skill is defensive, and most markdown backtick findings are false positives for documented Git commands, paths, or fenced examples. The real risks are the persistent Claude Code Bash hook and optional writes under ~/.claude, which can affect future sessions across projects. No prompt injection, network access, or secret exfiltration evidence was found.

remediation.suggestion: Default to project scope and require explicit user confirmation before writing to ~/.claude settings or hook paths.
Document the exact script path, required jq dependency, expected permissions, and verification result before enabling the hook.
Parse and merge existing Claude Code settings, then show the user the planned changes before saving.
Keep blocked patterns reviewed and test common bypass forms such as extra spacing, aliases, and chained commands.

content.user_title: Block Risky Git Commands in Claude Code
content.value_statement: Claude Code can run destructive Git commands if a workflow is not guarded. This skill installs a PreToolUse hook that blocks risky Git operations before execution.
actual_capabilities: Guides users through project or global Claude Code hook installation.
Copies a bundled Bash script into a .claude hooks path.
Configures a PreToolUse hook for Bash commands.
Blocks git push, hard reset, clean, branch deletion, and workspace restore patterns.
Provides a test flow to confirm blocked commands exit with code 2.
limitations: Requires bash, jq, and standard Unix shell tools.
Only checks command text against predefined patterns.
Does not replace Git branch protection, reviews, or backups.
Global installation affects every Claude Code project for the user.

use_cases.title: Protect a Shared Repository
use_cases.description: Add a project-level guardrail before using Claude Code in a repository with shared branches or release history.

use_cases.title: Add Personal Git Safeguards
use_cases.description: Reduce the chance of accidental pushes, hard resets, cleans, or branch deletions during AI-assisted development.

use_cases.title: Standardize AI Coding Workflows
use_cases.description: Use a repeatable hook setup for teams that want safer Claude Code behavior around destructive Git operations.

prompt_templates.title: Install Project Guardrails
prompt_templates.prompt: Set up this Git guardrail for the current project only. Ask before changing settings, then verify the hook works.

prompt_templates.title: Choose Installation Scope
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare project and global installation for this repository. Recommend the safer scope and explain which files would change.

prompt_templates.title: Customize Blocked Commands
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the default blocked Git command patterns and suggest additions for my team workflow. Explain the risk of removing safeguards.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Existing Hook Setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect my Claude Code hook configuration for Git safety coverage. Identify conflicts, missing patterns, and verification steps before changes.

output_examples.input: Install Git guardrails for this project.
output_examples.output: The skill asks for project scope, places the guardrail script under project Claude configuration, updates the Bash hook, and reports verification.

output_examples.input: Help my team block additional destructive Git operations.
output_examples.output: The skill reviews the default blocked patterns, suggests team-specific additions, and explains how each change affects normal Git workflows.

output_examples.input: Check whether my global setup is safe.
output_examples.output: The skill reviews the global hook configuration, warns about cross-project effects, and recommends project scope when global coverage is unnecessary.

best_practices: Prefer project installation when safeguards only apply to one repository.
Review global hooks before enabling them for all projects.
Keep blocked patterns aligned with your team Git policy.
anti_patterns: Installing global hooks without explaining the cross-project effect.
Overwriting existing Claude Code settings instead of merging hook entries.
Removing destructive Git patterns to bypass review or release controls.

faq.question: Is this skill only for Claude Code?
faq.answer: The hook setup is designed for Claude Code. Marketplace metadata also lists Claude and Codex for discovery and review workflows.

faq.question: Does it block every Git command?
faq.answer: No. It blocks selected destructive patterns, including push, hard reset, clean, branch deletion, and workspace restore commands.

faq.question: Can I install it for one project?
faq.answer: Yes. The project scope places settings and the hook under the repository Claude configuration.

faq.question: What does global installation change?
faq.answer: Global installation writes under ~/.claude and can affect every Claude Code project for that user.

faq.question: Does it protect Git outside Claude Code?
faq.answer: No. It is a Claude Code hook and does not enforce policy in terminals, CI systems, or Git hosting platforms.

faq.question: What tools does the hook require?
faq.answer: The bundled script expects bash, jq, grep, echo, and standard Unix shell behavior.
